study type: national, prospective, observational, population-based case series study
finding: The majority of women with macroprolactinomas and nonfunctioning adenomas experience good pregnancy outcomes, although nonfunctioning adenomas are more common in pregnancy than previously thought and may present de novo with symptoms of pituitary expansion during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Women with nonfunctioning adenomas were more likely to have a cesarean delivery than women in a control group (relative risk 2.06, 95% confidence interval 1.26–3.36, *P*=.035).
